name: Mog, Moogle Warrior
oracle_text:
Lifelink
Dance — At the beginning of your end step, each player may discard a card. Each player who discarded a card this way draws a card. If a creature card was discarded this way, you create a 1/2 white Moogle creature token with lifelink. Then if a noncreature card was discarded this way, put a +1/+1 counter on each Moogle you control.
blocked_sentences: If a creature card was discarded this way, you create a 1/2 white Moogle creature token with lifelink.
Then if a noncreature card was discarded this way, put a +1/+1 counter on each Moogle you control.

needs.what: a condition/value leaf that names the cards discarded during this ability's own resolution and filters them by card type, so an `if` can ask "was a creature card discarded this way" and "was a noncreature card discarded this way" — e.g. a `discarded_this_way` value taking a selector and returning a count, usable inside `cmp`/`exists`, populated by the `discard` op for the duration of the resolution (and across a `for_each_player` loop, since this card asks about every player's discard, not just the controller's)
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `discard` records nothing and returns nothing. `cards_to_graveyard_this_turn` is the closest value key and is wrong twice over: it is turn-scoped rather than resolution-scoped and it counts every graveyard at the table and every earlier discard, mill or death this turn. `count` over `{"zone": "graveyard"}` counts what was already there — in the verification sandbox that is two creature cards, so the creature branch would fire unconditionally. `connive` is the only op that reads its own discard, but it is a fused draw+discard+counter-on-self op with "nonland" hardcoded; it cannot gate an arbitrary effect, cannot ask about "creature" vs "noncreature", and cannot see another player's discard. Its own docstring states the case: "the cards that were just discarded, which nothing in the condition or value language can name".

needs.what: a 1/2 white Moogle creature token with lifelink in the token pool (id in the style of the existing entries, e.g. `moogle_1_2_w_lifelink`), so `create_token` has an id to name
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `create_token` only creates tokens already defined in data/cards/tokens.cards.json, and that file has no Moogle of any size — the nearest lifelink tokens are `vampire_1_1_b_lifelink`, `vampire_1_1_wb_lifelink` and `vampire_rogue_1_1_b_lifelink`, all 1/1 Vampires of the wrong subtype and colors. The subtype is load-bearing here, because the card's last clause puts counters on each Moogle you control.
